question: Has Workday announced any restructuring recently? What are the details and expected costs?
grading: Reference-free (no fixed answer), graded for recency and support. Expect: announced 2026-09-29; reorganizations including a reduction of approximately 2.5% of the workforce, primarily in Product and Technology, plus select leased office space reductions; estimated charges USD 65M-80M (about USD 55M-70M in Q3 FY2027 and about USD 10M in Q4 FY2027); fiscal 2027 Q3 and full-year guidance reiterated except GAAP operating margin. Snapshot as of 2026-10-03.
answer: On September 29, 2026 Workday disclosed in an 8-K (Items 2.02 and 2.05) that certain functions announced reorganizations including a reduction of approximately 2.5% of its workforce, primarily within the Product and Technology team, and select leased office space reductions, while continuing to hire in strategic areas. It estimates charges of about USD 65-80 million, of which about USD 55-70 million in Q3 FY2027 and about USD 10 million in Q4 FY2027 (roughly USD 40-55 million future cash for severance and benefits, about USD 10 million non-cash stock-based compensation and about USD 15 million non-cash lease impairment). Workday reiterated its Q3 and full-year FY2027 guidance from August 27 except GAAP operating margin (now about 20-21 points below non-GAAP in Q3 and about 19 points below for the full year). [T16-E1, T16-E2] Separately, on October 1, 2026 Workday entered into a new USD 1.5 billion revolving credit agreement replacing its USD 1.0 billion 2022 facility; this is not part of the restructuring. [T16-E3]

output.answer:
**Question:** Has Workday announced any restructuring recently? What are the details and expected costs?
*As of 2026-10-03*

**Interpreted as:** 'Recently' read as the current fiscal year to date (FY2027, began 2026-02-01), with emphasis on the latest reported quarter Q2 FY2027 (2026-05-01 to 2026-07-31) Workday read as Workday, Inc. (WDAY), the SEC registrant; fiscal year ends January 31, so FY2027 is the fiscal year in progress Question asks only for facts about an announced restructuring (scope, timing, expected costs) — no valuation, price or recommendation content

| | Amount (USD millions) | Workforce reduction | Total charges (USD millions) | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Total estimated charges | $65 million to $80 million [1] | — | — | — |
| Expected to be recognized in Q3 FY2027 (quarter ending October 31, 2026) | $55 million to $70 million [1] | — | — | — |
| Expected to be recognized in Q4 FY2027 (quarter ending January 31, 2027) | $10 million [1] | — | — | — |
| Future cash expenditures (severance payments, employee benefits, related costs) | $40 million to $55 million [1] | — | — | — |
| Non-cash stock-based compensation charges | $10 million [1] | — | — | — |
| Non-cash impairment of certain leased office space | $15 million [1] | — | — | — |
| Fiscal 2026 Restructuring Plan (announced February 2025) | — | approximately 7.5% of workforce [2] | $233 million ($196 million employee transition, severance, benefits and share-based compensation; $37 million office space impairment) [2] | Substantially completed in Q2 FY2026; no remaining liability as of January 31, 2026 [2] |
| Fiscal 2027 Restructuring Plan (announced February 2026) | — | approximately 2% of workforce [2] | $135 million in fiscal 2026 ($55 million employee transition, severance, benefits and share-based compensation; $80 million impairments of office space and certain long-lived assets) [2] | Substantially completed in Q1 FY2027; no material remaining liability as of July 31, 2026 (remaining liability was $41 million as of January 31, 2026); no material charges recorded in the three and six months ended July 31, 2026 [2] |
| September 2026 reorganization (announced September 29, 2026) | — | approximately 2.5% of current workforce, primarily Product and Technology [1] | $65 million to $80 million [1] | Announced September 29, 2026; employee actions expected substantially complete by Q1 FY2028, leased office space actions by Q4 FY2027 [1] |

- Yes — Workday announced a new reorganization on September 29, 2026, disclosed in an 8-K under Item 2.05 (Costs Associated with Exit or Disposal Activities). [1]
- The September 2026 reorganization includes a reduction of approximately 2.5% of Workday's current workforce, primarily within its Product and Technology team, plus select leased office space reductions. [1]
- Workday said it plans to continue hiring in key strategic areas and locations throughout fiscal 2027 despite the reduction. [1]
- The employee-related actions are expected to be substantially completed by the first quarter of fiscal 2028, subject to local law and consultation requirements, while the leased office space actions are expected to be substantially completed by the fourth quarter of fiscal 2027. [1]
- Workday said the charge estimates and timing are subject to assumptions including local law requirements in various jurisdictions, and that actual amounts may differ materially from estimates. [1]
- Because of the September 2026 reorganization, Workday now expects its fiscal 2027 third quarter GAAP operating margin to be approximately 20 to 21 percentage points lower than its third quarter non-GAAP operating margin, and its fiscal 2027 full-year GAAP operating margin to be approximately 19 percentage points lower than its full-year non-GAAP operating margin; it reiterated all other Q3 and full-year FY2027 guidance given on August 27, 2026. [1]
- Workday intends to exclude the charges associated with the September 2026 reorganization from its non-GAAP financial measures. [1]
- Workday's most recent quarterly report (Q2 FY2027, quarter ended July 31, 2026) recorded no material restructuring expenses: restructuring costs were $0 in both the three and six months ended July 31, 2026, versus $1 million and $167 million in the prior-year periods. [2][3]
- Separately from the restructuring plans, Workday's Q2 FY2027 diluted net income per share included a tax benefit of $1.52 per share related to an intra-entity transfer of certain intellectual property rights as part of an internal legal entity restructuring — a legal-entity matter, not a workforce restructuring plan. [3]
- Secondary news coverage reported the September 2026 action as affecting about 525 employees, or roughly 500 positions, and as Workday's second workforce reduction of 2026. [4][5]
- Note a discrepancy: two secondary sources (LatestLY and The American Bazaar) reported the expected charges as $65 million to $85 million, whereas Workday's own 8-K states approximately $65 million to $80 million; the company filing is the authoritative figure. [5][4][1]

**Not available**
- Actual charges recognized to date under the September 2026 reorganization (as opposed to estimated charges): The reorganization was announced September 29, 2026, within Q3 FY2027 (quarter ending October 31, 2026), which is still in progress and not yet reported; Workday's Q3 FY2027 results are expected November 27, 2026 per secondary coverage, and no actual charge amounts have been disclosed. [1][4]
- Number of employees affected, as stated by Workday: Workday's 8-K discloses only a percentage (approximately 2.5% of current workforce); the ~525 employee figure comes from secondary news reports, not from the company. [1][4]

**Sources**
[1] Workday, Inc. 8-K current report, items 2.02,2.05 (filed 2026-09-29) 8-K (www.sec.gov, 2026-09-29, primary) https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1327811/000132781126000048/wday-20260929.htm
[2] Workday, Inc. 10-Q for Q2 FY2027 (filed 2026-08-27) (www.sec.gov, 2026-08-27, primary) https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1327811/000132781126000044/wday-20260731.htm
[3] Workday, Inc. earnings release for Q2 FY2027, 8-K EX-99.1 (filed 2026-08-27) (www.sec.gov, 2026-08-27, primary) https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1327811/000132781126000042/wday-07312026x991.htm
[4] Workday to cut 2.5% of workforce, affecting about 525 employees - The American Bazaar (americanbazaaronline.com, 2026-09-30, secondary) https://americanbazaaronline.com/2026/09/30/workday-to-cut-2-5-of-workforce-affecting-about-525-employees-489102/
[5] Workday Layoffs: SaaS Provider Eliminating 500 Jobs in 2nd Workforce Reduction in 2026 - LatestLY (www.latestly.com, 2026-09-30, secondary) https://www.latestly.com/business/workday-layoffs-saas-provider-eliminating-500-jobs-in-2nd-workforce-reduction-in-2026-7626482.html
